findings.summary: The middle panel's legend is drawn over its own data. The iron-share plateau is a teal line at row 548 spanning columns 108 to 762, and the legend placed at lower right (scripts/iron_field_source/figure.py:109, loc=lower right) puts its third entry at exactly that row: the handle occupies rows 545-548 and the words Fh plane occupy rows 540-553 at columns 684-762, with the teal line visible through the letter gaps and across the lower half of the glyphs. The same defect is in the byte-identical twin at docs/figures/iron-core-magnetisation/icm-iron-field-source/west-62751-iron-stray-field.png. A reader cannot read the entry that names the third plane, and the legend ceases to say which colour is which exactly where all three series coincide.

The same three-entry plane legend is drawn twice on one figure, here in the upper panel (line 62) and again in the middle panel (line 109), and never in the lower panel, although the colours mean the same plane in every panel. One figure-level legend would carry the information once; the second copy is also what places a legend in the lower-right region the plateau occupies, which is the cause of the blocking collision above.

After the near-edge peak the three with-iron curves coincide to within about a pixel, so the upper panel's three-colour legend promises a comparison a reader cannot see: the panel carries 133 blue and 139 orange pixels against 1389 teal, and beyond column 200 only 56 blue and 56 orange pixels remain, where the lines are drawn underneath the teal one. The coincidence is the data rather than a plotting error, but the picture gives the impression that two series are missing; a note stating that the three planes coincide in the far field, or plotting the two hidden series dashed and offset-free, would let a reader tell agreement from absence.

The lower panel's y-axis label says (bars) for |B_air|, but the air-core marks are drawn with the horizontal-dash marker '_' (line 127) and render as short grey dashes and small squares, not as bars. A reader who wants the air-core value looks for the wrong mark and may take the dashes for a third series; the label should name the marks as drawn, or the marks should become bars.
